name: Attribution Reporting API (retired)
plain: Browser measured which ad click led to a purchase. Deprecated Chrome 144; removal under way in 2026.
meaning: Matched ad clicks or views to later conversions with noised event reports (3 bits click data for views) or encrypted aggregate reports. Google retired it in Oct 2025 and plans a W3C PATWG attribution standard instead.

access.persistence: Source lifetimes up to 30 days; reports delayed 2 days to 30 days
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

firefox.note: Firefox shipped a different PPA attribution experiment

safari.note: Private Click Measurement is Safari's separate API

limits.headline: Can't measure which ad click led to a purchase in Chrome anymore
limits.user_action: Nothing. It used to happen after an ad click and a later purchase
can: Have linked an ad click to a later purchase in Chrome, without a cookie
Have sent a report with limited detail after a delay
cannot: Run in Chrome 144 or later, where it is deprecated and being removed in 2026
Run in Edge or Samsung Internet
Name you in the report; it was built to be limited
Link a click to a purchase on a device without the feature
limits.reach_label: Retired, one click and one report
limits.differs: Chrome is removing it. Safari and Firefox have their own partial versions.

story.what_it_is: A Chrome tool that measured which ad led to a sale, with some noise added. Being removed.

marketing.name: Attribution Reporting
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitched it as ad measurement without cross site IDs, with noisy event reports and encrypted summaries.

story.for_you: You never saw it work. When you clicked an ad and bought, Chrome could send a fuzzy report instead of a name. It is now being removed, so most ad measurement goes back to cookies and server events.
story.for_makers: It was Google's answer to counting sales without following people. Fuzzy numbers kept identity out. Advertisers disliked the noise and the work, and Google retired it in 2025 and plans a new standard through a web group.

use_cases.example: An ad network counted sales from a banner on a news site, with random noise, so no single buyer was named.
A shop got a daily total of clicks that led to purchases for each ad, instead of a person by person list.
A fashion brand learned which ad format drove sales, with privacy noise added to small groups.
A mobile game maker's web ads could report installs and sign ups tied to a campaign, without a device ID.
A publisher showed advertisers proof that an ad on its site led to a sale, in aggregate only.
Fraud teams worried that noisy reports hid fake clicks, one reason many advertisers did not adopt it.

risks: Being removed, so measurement moves elsewhere

technical_bounds: Event reports carry 1 bit (views) or 3 bits (clicks) of conversion data
Reports delayed by hours to days
Cannot link to a cross-site identity

history.change: Stub in 152; removal per Chrome 153 release notes; no blink-dev update since 2026-07-02 as of Oct 2026 review
